Financing page includes an input to specify salvage value.

## Utility Projects[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#utility-projects "Link to this heading")

New models for utility financing options allowing specification of power purchase price as an input, and use of energy payment allocation factors to model time-of-use pricing.

New inputs on the Financing page for specifying construction interest costs that accrue before the analysis period begins.

Financing page includes an input to specify salvage value.

## Photovoltaic Systems[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#photovoltaic-systems "Link to this heading")

Array sizing calculator allows you to specify the system DC capacity, and automatically calculates the values for modules per string, strings in parallel, and number of inverters on the Array page.

Improved array shading model allows specification of beam shading factors using a table of 8,760 hourly values, a 24 by 12 month by hour table, or an azimuth by altitude table. Other options are to import shading data from the PVsyst simulation software or the SunEye shading analysis too. Finally the new shading model allows modeling of self-shading within the array (without backtracking).

Detailed derate factors can be specified directly on the Array page.

Improved error checking to help ensure inverter and array capacities are matched.

Updated module and inverter databases.

The electric storage (battery) model has been removed in this version.

Array page allows specification of the land area as a multiple of the total module area for reference. (Land area is not accounted for in cost calculations.)

New option for using updated Perez model for calculating incident radiation from data in weather file.

Fixed a problem with the way SAM calculated inverter AC output for hours when the DC input exceeded the inverter capacity.

Removed reference variables for CEC module model.

## Power Tower Systems[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#power-tower-systems "Link to this heading")

Improvement of condenser modeling in power block.

New cavity receiver model.

Add hybrid cooling.

Renaming of input and output variables for clarity.

Improved modeling of parasitic losses.

Add storage bypass valve control.

Receiver maximum flow rate based on HTF properties and maximum over design operation fraction.

New solar multiple input variable.

New receiver control variables.

Added specification of the land area as a multiple of the total module area for reference. (Land area is not accounted for in cost calculations.)

## Parabolic Trough Systems[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#parabolic-trough-systems "Link to this heading")

Improvement of condenser modeling in power block. (physical model)

Added specification of the land area as a multiple of the total module area for reference. (Land area is not accounted for in cost calculations.)

Improved modeling of fossil fuel usage for systems with fossil backup.

Add hybrid cooling. (physical model)

Improved heat loss calculation. (empirical model)

## Generic Solar System[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#generic-solar-system-1 "Link to this heading")

Added new model to facilitate modeling of concentrating solar power systems not handled by parabolic trough, power tower, and dish-Stirling models. Allows modeling of solar field based on a table of efficiency values.

## Geothermal Power Systems[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#geothermal-power-systems "Link to this heading")

New model for utility-scale geothermal power generation projects based on the U.S. DOE’s GETEM model.

## Small Scale Wind Systems[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#small-scale-wind-systems "Link to this heading")

New model for small wind systems that consist of one or more turbines for residential and commercial projects. Current version relies on wind speed data in solar TMY data.

# SAM 2010.4.12: April 2010 (Update)[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#sam-2010-4-12-april-2010-update "Link to this heading")

## This update corrects several issues with SAM 2010.3.31.:[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#this-update-corrects-several-issues-with-sam-2010-3-31 "Link to this heading")

System summary: Units for the total installed cost per capacity were incorrect for photovoltaic, solar water heating, and generic systems.

Financing: Projects with commercial or utility financing and an analysis period less than the depreciation period caused simulations to fail. (This was also true for previous versions.)

Incentives: Production-based incentives (PBI), production tax credits (PTC), and investment tax credits (ITC) were incorrectly calculated.

Photovoltaic systems: The annual energy production was incorrect for systems with bipolar inverters from the Sandia inverter database.

Solar water heating: System energy savings were incorrectly calculated.

Parabolic trough (physical): Receiver heat loss calculation was incorrect for receivers with lost vacuum or hydrogen leakage.

Power tower: Water usage was incorrectly reported, values of the solar field delivered energy and power block input energy were incorrectly reported in the hourly results worksheet, and default values of some input variables were incorrect.

Parabolic trough and power tower: Power block capacity-based costs were incorrectly calculated based on the net capacity instead of the gross capacity.

## The update includes the following improvements:[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#the-update-includes-the-following-improvements "Link to this heading")

Several new functions and improvements to the SamUL scripting language, including the ability to run scripts from the command line.

Revised user documentation.

# SAM 2010.3.31: March 2010[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#sam-2010-3-31-march-2010 "Link to this heading")

This version adds a solar water heating model and a new parabolic trough model to Solar Advisor, improves the display of graphs on the results page, and adds capabilities to the statistical analysis simulation option. It also includes interface improvements to the photovoltaic module and inverter pages, improves modeling of temperature effects on module performance, and includes the latest module and inverter databases from the CEC and Sandia. Finally, this version adds a weather data download feature for U.S. locations, and a function to create weather files in TMY3 format.

## General New Features[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#general-new-features-1 "Link to this heading")

New solar water heating model for residential systems.

Tax credits and incentives can be defined as annual schedules.

Add levelized cost of energy (LCOE) with and without incentives.

New functions in SamUL

Graph thumbnails on Results page.

Input window for loads (photovoltaic, solar water heating) adds options for specifying load data: Daily profiles by month, cut and paste from clipboard.

## Weather Data[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#weather-data-4 "Link to this heading")

Location lookup option automatically downloads NREL Solar Prospector weather data for U.S. locations using an address or latitude and longitude.

TMY3 creator facilitates creating custom weather files.

## PV[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#pv-1 "Link to this heading")

Simple load and storage models added to all photovoltaic models. Was only available in PVWatts model in previous versions.

Revised default rating conditions for concentrating photovoltaic (CPV) model. This will affect capacity-based calculations including LCOE when the module cost is specified in $/W.

Temperature correction added to concentrating photovoltaic (CPV) model, and improved in simple efficiency and Sandia models to include more options for specifying mounting options.

Improved layout of Module page for CEC and Sandia model. Display I-V curve and other changes.

Improved layout of Inverter page. Display inverter efficiency curves and rename input variables.

Azimuth tracking option added to photovoltaic models.

New hourly output data columns added to hourly outputs.

Corrected system performance factor calculation for systems with shading.

## Parabolic Trough[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#parabolic-trough "Link to this heading")

New physical model for parabolic trough systems. Original trough model renamed empirical trough model. Both trough models are available in the current version.

## Power Tower[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#power-tower-2 "Link to this heading")

New field land area variables on Heliostat Field page.

Variables on input pages reorganized.

## Generic Fossil[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#generic-fossil "Link to this heading")

Allow generic fossil input variables to be parametric variables.

# Version 2009.10.2: October 2009[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#version-2009-10-2-october-2009 "Link to this heading")

## General New Features[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#general-new-features-2 "Link to this heading")

Significantly faster model runs and smaller project file sizes.

Both Windows and Mac OS X-Intel versions are available.

A SCIF file importer for opening files saved with previous versions of SAM.

A new graphs page can display up to four graphs simultaneously and has new controls for creating and modifying graphs.

Tornado-chart type analysis is built-in as a specific Sensitivity analysis.

Optimization allows you to maximize or minimize a metric with respect to inputs.

Multiple sub-systems allows you to model systems made up of two or more subsystems.

Weather model reads TMY3, EPW, and TMY2 files.

Scripting and batch-mode capabilities with Excel and other programming languages.

## PV[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#pv-2 "Link to this heading")

Update CEC module database (10/2)

Simple Efficiency Model allows for multiple radiation level/efficiency pairs (Flat Plate and CPV)

Incorporated PVWatts model

## Dish-Stirling[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#dish-stirling "Link to this heading")

No updates.

## Parabolic Trough[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#parabolic-trough-1 "Link to this heading")

Update HCE library.

Improvements to thermal storage dispatch strategies.

Can accept custom HTF fluids using a table-lookup mechanism.

## Power Tower[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#power-tower-3 "Link to this heading")

Improved heliostat layout mechanism and optimization wizard.

Can accept custom HTF fluids using a table-lookup mechanism.

# Version 3.0: June 2009[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#version-3-0-june-2009 "Link to this heading")

## New Features[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#new-features "Link to this heading")

Power tower model.

## PV[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#pv-3 "Link to this heading")

Simple array shading model.

Add energy flow graph to standard graphs on Results page.

Update Sandia inverter database.

Update CEC module database.

## Dish-Stirling[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#dish-stirling-1 "Link to this heading")

No updates.

## Parabolic Trough[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#parabolic-trough-2 "Link to this heading")

Update HCE library.

Tracking of backup boiler fuel cost in cash flow and cost of energy calculations.

Improve calculation of backup boiler fuel usage.

## General[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#general-15 "Link to this heading")

Updated help system and user guide, including topics for power tower model.

## Minor changes[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#minor-changes "Link to this heading")

Update and rename sample files.

Improvements to user-defined variable implementation.

For cases using Excel optimization (utility financing model), Excel file runs in background by default.

Improve handing of SCIF files.

Show incentive tax details by default on Incentives page.

General improvements to speed up run times.

# Version 2.5: November 2008[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#version-2-5-november-2008 "Link to this heading")

## New Features[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#new-features-1 "Link to this heading")

Parabolic dish-Stirling engine model.

Time-of-use utility rates.

User documentation available as both context-sensitive Help and PDF file.

Automated optimization of power purchase agreement (PPA) price escalation rate and load fraction for projects with IPP and Utility financing.

## PV[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#pv-4 "Link to this heading")

Revise inverter and array sizes in sample file.

Update Sandia inverter database.

Update CEC module database.

Change module and inverter database format to Excel from MDB.

Display voltage and capacity variables on array page to facilitate inverter and array sizing.

## Dish-Stirling[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#dish-stirling-2 "Link to this heading")

Add dish-Stirling sample file.

Implement dish-Stirling model.

## Parabolic Trough[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#parabolic-trough-3 "Link to this heading")

Remove unused variables from user interface: number of receivers per SCA, HTF flow control, HTF night flow control, and turbine start-up time.

Rename time-of-use variables to time-of-dispatch and move them from Utility page to Storage page.

## General[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#general-16 "Link to this heading")

Remove Utility - IOU option from list of financing types on Financials page, and rename Utility - IPP option to IPP and Utility .

Improve graphing options.

Change utility rate units from cents/kWh to $/kWh.

Add Excel-based optimization of PPA escalation rate and debt fraction for IPP and Utility financing.

Improve installation on Windows Vista.

Improve sliders interface.

## Minor changes[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#minor-changes-1 "Link to this heading")

Fix time format issue with parabolic trough time of dispatch schedule.

Improve file compression to minimize file size.

Allow long variable names in parametric analyses.

Revise WACC calculation.

Read all significant digits from linked spreadsheets.

# Version 2.0: June 2008[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#version-2-0-june-2008 "Link to this heading")

## PV[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#pv-5 "Link to this heading")

Implement new inverter performance model: Sandia Performance Model for Grid-connected PV Inverters

Removed previous curve-fit inverter model

Implement new photovoltaic module performance model: California Energy Commission Performance Model.

Update Sandia PV Array Performance Model with additional modules. (Was King Model in previous versions.)

## CSP[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#csp "Link to this heading")

Implement dry cooling capability for CSP systems.

Add new Solel UVAC3 HCE to CSP model library.

## General[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#general-17 "Link to this heading")

Add generic technology option: The simple heat-rate model allows comparisons between solar technologies and conventional fuel-based technologies in all markets.

Add Third Party Ownership option to commercial projects.

Allow operation and maintenance costs and annual degradation rates to be entered on a year-by-year basis.

Add new results workbook that stores complete set of calculated metrics, hourly data, monthly averages, and annual averages to facilitate reviewing results in Excel.

Improve display of results page: Move results button to bottom of navigation menu; replace single button with three, Results Summary, Spreadsheet, and Time Series Graph; implement new Run Analysis button to replace results pending status. Also add new Results menu.

Replace LCOE stacked bar graph with stacked cost graph to correct error in LCOE cost breakdown under certain conditions.

Add several new standard graphs, including monthly output, monthly inverter efficiency (PV only), and energy flow (CSP only).

Add new graphs that are available when one or more Independent parametric groups are defined.

Create new compressed file format (SCIF) that stores only inputs in small files for easier file sharing. Cases can be imported and exported from SAM files in the SCIF format.

## Minor changes[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#minor-changes-2 "Link to this heading")

Minor bug fixes

Reduce required disk storage space by deleting workbooks and other files from temporary folder when closing SAM.

Add transformer derate category to Array page for PV systems.

Display weighted average cost of capital (WACC) on Financials page.

Improve internal rate of return (IRR) calculation for utility and third party ownership projects.

New Fixed (per year) operation and maintenance category.

New folder (Samples\\Financial\_Spreadsheets) contains sample workbooks illustrating Solar Advisor financial calculations. Workbooks are also posted on the Solar Advisor website.

Solar Advisor opens with an empty window instead of automatically opening previous file.

Add close file button to menu bar.

# Version 1.3: October 16, 2007[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#version-1-3-october-16-2007 "Link to this heading")

## General[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#general-18 "Link to this heading")

Add capability to use EnergyPlus Weather file format (EPW) files for weather data.

Add capability to add weather files to the collection of built-in files.

Add weather data viewing tools, links to weather data web sites, and Help button to the Climate page.

Add ground reflectance with snow input variable to Array page for PV systems. SAM Applies the snow ground reflectance value during hours that the weather data indicates there is snow on the ground.

Fix a bug in the inverter model for low part-load operation.

Add waterfall graph capability in DView on Results page for CSP systems.

Update user guide.

Improve overall performance of model.

## Other changes[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#other-changes "Link to this heading")

Add start up mode settings (File, Settings) and change tab names in Settings window.

Add help button to Climate page that opens a help page describing weather file options.

Improve search algorithm that finds a solution for systems using utility financing.

Improve calculation of number of TRNSYS runs displayed in information message.

Change hourly output buttons on Results page for CSP systems.

Improve handling of files created by different versions of SAM.

Improve automatic graph scaling.

Improve message for users attempting to run SAM when the Windows language setting is not English.

Improve automatic scale on sliders.

Improve file navigation for File, Open and File, Save As commands.

# Version 1.1: August 10, 2007[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#version-1-1-august-10-2007 "Link to this heading")

## General[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#general-19 "Link to this heading")

Photovoltaics Array: Add detailed derate factors.

Results: Add Slider column to results summary table that displays output measures based on the position of visible sliders.

## Results[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#results "Link to this heading")

Change the units of ITC and IBI incentives that appear with sliders and in graphs from % Max to %.

Improve the functioning of the Notes box.

For utility systems with IOU financing, remove first year PPA from the results summary table.

For utility IPP financing, improve the LCOE calculation algorithm.

## Incentives[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#incentives "Link to this heading")

Cursor changes to an hourglass while resetting default market values.

Correct default settings for tax details to show that for residential systems, all utility incentives are taxable, and that utility incentives do not reduce the ITC basis.

## Photovoltaics Array[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#photovoltaics-array "Link to this heading")

Changed default total derate factor in sample files to 84% to match PVWATTS.

## Costs[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#costs "Link to this heading")

Correct the way the sales tax rate and module cost per unit values are displayed.

## Parametrics[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#parametrics "Link to this heading")

Fixed a bug related to incentives.

Fixed a bug related user-defined variables.

## External Spreadsheets[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#external-spreadsheets "Link to this heading")

Improved handling of missing workbooks.

Fixed a bug related to working with external spreadsheets.

## Menus[#](https://natlabrockies.github.io/SAM/doc/reference/release_notes.html#menus "Link to this heading")

Add the Release notes command to Help menu to display a list of version numbers and the new features and fixes associated with each version number.

Reorganize the list of commands on the Case menu.

How to customize electricity usage 
OpenSolar Support 
May 08, 2026 17:45
Updated
Follow 
Summary
OpenSolar enables you to tailor your customer’s electricity usage data to ensure highly accurate proposals. You can input electricity usage manually, estimate it, or derive it from bills. Additional settings allow you to shape daily usage profiles, adjust weekend usage scaling, and account for demand and controlled loads. This guide walks you through the full customization process.
Table of Contents
Selecting Electricity Usage
Shaping Electricity Usage Profile
Scaling Weekend vs. Weekday Usage
Setting Demand Using 8760 Values
Setting Controlled Loads
Video walkthrough
Selecting Electricity Usage:
To begin, open your desired project and go to the Energy tab. At the top, you’ll find the Electricity Usage section.
Use the Data Source dropdown to select the most suitable input method based on available information:
Options for Usage Input:
Data Source Description 
OpenSolar Usage Estimates	Use if no customer usage/bill data is available. Choose: 
- Estimate (Low) 
- Estimate (Medium) (Default) 
- Estimate (High) 	
Enter kWh Usage	Use if actual usage is known. Options include: 
- Daily Consumption (Monthly avg) 
- Monthly Consumption 
- Quarterly Consumption 
- Annual Consumption 
- Hourly Interval Data (15/30/60-min intervals)	
Enter Electricity Bill	If bills are available and a tariff is set: 
- Annual Bill 
- Quarterly Bills 
- Monthly Bills 
- Bi-monthly Bill
Usage is interpolated based on the selected tariff.	
Note: Missing monthly or quarterly data is automatically interpolated by OpenSolar.
Shaping Electricity Usage Profile:
This step is optional unless you're using hourly interval data.
Once usage is entered, expand Advanced Settings and toggle Configure Usage Profile Curves to define weekday and weekend usage patterns.
Choose a usage curve for weekdays and another for weekends.
A live graph displays the selected curve shape.
If no curve is selected, the system defaults to Evening Peak.
OpenSolar offers a library of common daily energy profile shapes for various user behaviors.
Scaling Weekend vs. Weekday Usage:
You can fine-tune weekend usage relative to weekdays:
Example: If weekend usage is 10% higher than weekday, enter 1.1.
For 50% higher usage, enter 1.5.
This impacts TOU (Time of Use) calculations and solar self-consumption accuracy.
Setting Demand Using 8760 Values:
Recommended for accurate demand charge calculations.
If demand is not explicitly set, OpenSolar assumes maximum hourly usage equals hourly demand, which is often inaccurate.
To address this:
Upload 15, 30, or 60-minute interval data for an entire year (8760 hours).
See detailed instructions for uploading interval data →
Setting Controlled Loads:
If the household has controlled loads (e.g., water heater):
Expand Advanced Settings.
Toggle on Set Controlled Loads.
Enter daily usage (in kWh) for up to 3 devices under Controlled Load 1, 2, 3.
Default behavior distributes controlled load usage between 12:00 AM – 5:00 AM.
Final Step: Save Your Changes:
Make sure to save all your changes before exiting the Energy tab to ensure accurate calculations in the proposal.
Video walkthrough:

At the top, you’ll find the **Electricity Usage** section. Use the **Data Source** dropdown to select the most suitable input method based on available information: ![Screenshot 2025-09-17 at 10.44.17 am.png](/hc/article_attachments/13791406552847) #### Options for Usage Input: | **Data Source** | **Description** | | --- | --- | | **OpenSolar Usage Estimates** | Use if no customer usage/bill data is available. Choose: 
\- _Estimate (Low)_ 
\- _Estimate (Medium)_ _(Default)_ 
\- _Estimate (High)_ | | **Enter kWh Usage** | Use if actual usage is known. Options include: 
\- _Daily Consumption (Monthly avg)_ 
\- _Monthly Consumption_ 
\- _Quarterly Consumption_ 
\- _Annual Consumption_ 
\- _Hourly Interval Data_ (15/30/60-min intervals) | | **Enter Electricity Bill** | If bills are available and a tariff is set: 
\- _Annual Bill_ 
\- _Quarterly Bills_ 
\- _Monthly Bills_ 
\- _Bi-monthly Bill_
Usage is interpolated based on the selected tariff. | _Note: Missing monthly or quarterly data is automatically interpolated by OpenSolar._ ## Shaping Electricity Usage Profile: > _This step is optional unless you're using hourly interval data._ Once usage is entered, expand **Advanced Settings** and toggle **Configure Usage Profile Curves** to define weekday and weekend usage patterns. * Choose a usage curve for weekdays and another for weekends. * A live graph displays the selected curve shape. * If no curve is selected, the system defaults to **Evening Peak**. ![Screenshot 2025-09-17 at 10.42.30 am.png](/hc/article_attachments/13791415318543) OpenSolar offers a library of common daily energy profile shapes for various user behaviors. ![mceclip1.png](/hc/article_attachments/13183754585871) ## Scaling Weekend vs. Weekday Usage: You can fine-tune weekend usage relative to weekdays: * Example: If weekend usage is 10% higher than weekday, enter `1.1`. * For 50% higher usage, enter `1.5`. This impacts TOU (Time of Use) calculations and solar self-consumption accuracy. ![Screenshot 2025-09-17 at 10.46.17 am.png](/hc/article_attachments/13791406553359) ## Setting Demand Using 8760 Values: > _Recommended for accurate demand charge calculations._ If demand is not explicitly set, OpenSolar assumes maximum hourly usage equals hourly demand, which is often inaccurate. To address this: * Upload 15, 30, or 60-minute interval data for an entire year (8760 hours). * [See detailed instructions for uploading interval data →](https://support.opensolar.com/hc/en-us/articles/13183763473295-How-to-customize-electricity-usage#) ## Setting Controlled Loads: If the household has controlled loads (e.g., water heater): 1. Expand **Advanced Settings**. 2. Toggle on **Set Controlled Loads**. 3. Enter daily usage (in kWh) for up to 3 devices under _Controlled Load 1, 2, 3_. _Default behavior distributes controlled load usage between 12:00 AM – 5:00 AM._ ![Screenshot 2025-09-17 at 10.47.45 am.png](/hc/article_attachments/13791406553743) ### Final Step: Save Your Changes: Make sure to **save** all your changes before exiting the Energy tab to ensure accurate calculations in the proposal. ## Video walkthrough: ### Related articles * [How to select the correct electricity utility/tariff](https://support.opensolar.com/hc/en-us/related/click?data=BAh7CjobZGVzdGluYXRpb25fYXJ0aWNsZV9pZGwrCA%2BM%2BJD9CzoYcmVmZXJyZXJfYXJ0aWNsZV9pZGwrCI%2FjiZX9CzoLbG9jYWxlSSIKZW4tdXMGOgZFVDoIdXJsSSJbL2hjL2VuLXVzL2FydGljbGVzLzEzMTgzNjg2ODM5MzExLUhvdy10by1zZWxlY3QtdGhlLWNvcnJlY3QtZWxlY3RyaWNpdHktdXRpbGl0eS10YXJpZmYGOwhUOglyYW5raQY%3D--4b29c1f724d560df11cfbfe9a9cfbd77fb7879d6) Data Formats:
OpenSolar accepts the following configurations:
Data Structures: Vertical or Horizontal

# How to upload interval data

![](https://support.opensolar.com/system/photos/8966678827023/OS_logo.png)

[OpenSolar Support](https://support.opensolar.com/hc/en-us/profiles/903548256586-OpenSolar-Support)

*   May 08, 2026 17:59
*   Updated

[Follow](https://support.opensolar.com/hc/en-us/articles/13183853699215-How-to-upload-interval-data/subscription.html "Opens a sign-in dialog")

## Summary:

Uploading interval data is the most accurate way to model a customer’s energy consumption and calculate potential solar savings. OpenSolar supports 15, 30, and 60-minute interval data in CSV format and accommodates both **vertical** and **horizontal** data structures. This guide walks you through how to upload, configure, and manage interval data within your project.

## Table of contents:

*   [Uploading Interval Data](https://support.opensolar.com/hc/en-us/articles/13183853699215-How-to-upload-interval-data#h_01JZK4Z81DD3E94C7K5EJ4QX3C)
*   [Data Formats](https://support.opensolar.com/hc/en-us/articles/13183853699215-How-to-upload-interval-data#h_01JZK4Z81G41D0458TD96HB0XG)
*   [Preparing the Data Before You Upload](https://support.opensolar.com/hc/en-us/articles/13183853699215-How-to-upload-interval-data#h_01JZK4Z81KMRX05FJYCBXYSMKD)
*   [Video Walkthrough](https://support.opensolar.com/hc/en-us/articles/13183853699215-How-to-upload-interval-data#h_01JZK4Z81PFVWT2ZDEY8RE85BX)

## Uploading Interval Data:

*   Open your desired **Project** in OpenSolar.
*   Navigate to the **Energy** tab.
*   In the **Electricity Usage** section, select **“Interval Data”** from the **Data Source** dropdown.
*   Select the **Upload CSV** button

![](/hc/article_attachments/13183853698831)

## Data Formats:

OpenSolar accepts the following configurations:

*   **Data Structures**: Vertical or Horizontal
*   **Interval Durations**: 15-minute, 30-minute, or 60-minute intervals

The only files that can be added are our templates that can be downloaded from the Upload CSV window:

![](/hc/article_attachments/13183853698959)

## Preparing the Data Before You Upload:

When you download one of our templates, these can not be edited. The file uploaded must have the same headers as when you download it, or the information will be incorrect.

If your usage information starts on 06/12, find the row 06/12 on our template and place the usage information there. 

*   **Partial Datasets Are Accepted**: You do not need a full calendar year (January–December). The system supports data that:
    *   Spans across years (e.g., June 2024 to May 2025)
    *   Covers less than 12 months
*   **Automatic Extrapolation**: Missing data will be intelligently filled by OpenSolar’s algorithm to estimate full-year values.
*   **Flexible Units**: After uploading, you’ll be prompted to confirm or adjust the unit of measurement used in the file.
*   **Processing Time**: Large datasets, especially at 15-minute intervals, may take slightly longer to process—please be patient.
